dossiers.title: Arma 3
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Arma 3 plays as an unusually deliberate military simulation with long sight lines, lethal firefights, detailed infantry controls and meaningful preparation rather than rapid arcade shooting.
The same base game supports authored solo scenarios, editor-made missions and very different organized multiplayer formats, so the activity structure depends substantially on chosen server or group.

Coordinated teams and player-run milsim events allow unusually immersive, long tactical operations, while the quality and accessibility of sessions depend on compatible groups, servers, scenarios and mods.

Rather than relying on a linear leveling system, extended play tends to develop the player's tactical skill, scenario-making abilities and familiarity with complex equipment and workshop modifications.
Detailed key bindings, slower movement and complex situational procedures create a steep learning curve; new or solo players may struggle without practicing or consulting community guides.
The scenario editor and workshop can dramatically transform objectives, eras, maps and rules, giving the sandbox more replay variety than the built-in campaign alone.
Player accounts include awkward companion AI in scripted missions, sensitivity to community mod compatibility and variable performance in heavily scripted multiplayer situations.
Believable combined-arms scenarios and large environments are repeatedly valued, although some participants find movement and vehicle handling comparatively clunky.
Much of the pleasure comes from planning, positioning and emergent group stories; substantial mission preparation and slow travel can make this feel unlike a conventional rapid-action campaign.

conflicts.statement: The ability to stage rich personalized operations is praised as unique, while heavy technical, preparation and group coordination demands are described as obstacles by other players.

dossiers.title: Roguebook
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Two heroes fight as one party using shared card play, gems and positional swaps that change who takes damage and which attacks are most effective.
The player uncovers a hex-tile map using ink and brushes, making the selection of fights, rewards and routes an exploration resource-management choice rather than a fixed ladder.
Cards, embedded gems, artifacts, talents and unlocked heroes produce different party builds, with run modifiers and post-run progression offering longer-term experimentation.

Players disagree about the tactical balance: some find the learning curve approachable and difficulty well judged, while others report punishing random encounters, uneven builds or overly luck-dependent openings.
The relatively small fixed world and encounter selection can feel repetitive over many attempts despite changing card synergies and selectable higher-difficulty conditions.
Several players enjoy long runs that let carefully composed decks develop, but others feel slow meta progression and multiple similar battles overextend the experience.
The colorful hand-drawn fantasy presentation, sound effects and music are prominent recurring positives even in reviews that are ambivalent about combat and replayability.
World-building and story material are comparatively light; for many players the attraction lies primarily in party tactics and exploration rather than character-driven narrative.

Player feedback highlights occasional readability or navigation limitations on some displays and reports of isolated interface or translation faults, with reports from different historical versions rather than proven present-day issues.

conflicts.statement: Some reviewers describe creative builds and map exploration as highly replayable, while others regard limited encounter variety, balance swings and slow unlocks as reasons the runs wear thin.

dossiers.title: Dry Drowning
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The story is a choice-driven dystopian noir visual novel following a discredited investigator, combining lengthy dialogue with clues, interrogations and occasional exploration or evidence use.
Players inspect locations and evidence, select dialogue responses and interrogate suspects; the investigative puzzles are accessible, but action or traditional adventure mechanics are limited.
The striking dark illustrated aesthetic and atmospheric soundtrack receive strong praise, including from players who disliked parts of the story or its pacing.
Frequent conversations, extensive exposition and required supporting documents build the fictional world but can interrupt narrative momentum and make the plot feel overly wordy.
Some readers find the mystery and morally charged political setting engrossing, while others judge the plot convoluted or characters shallow by the middle acts.
Choice points can change relationships, branch outcomes and endings, encouraging rereads, yet reviewers differ on whether those branches significantly reshape the core story.

Players report the long reading requirement and interruptions to conversation as the dominant interaction cost; older accounts additionally mention restricted save timing or lack of text-skipping convenience.
A Russian-language player reviewing the original 2019 release found the detective prose challenging in English and specifically regretted the absence of Russian localization.
Replaying for alternate outcomes can expose different scenes, but long shared portions of dialogue and relatively simple clue interactions limit the variety between playthroughs.

conflicts.statement: Some players experience consequential dialogue branches and meaningful alternate endings, whereas others describe a predominantly linear novel whose choices change less than expected.
